title: Lumbar puncture in the febrile infant under 60 days
alt: Flowchart: an ill, preterm or under-8-day infant needs full evaluation including lumbar puncture. From 8 to 28 days the puncture is routine. From 29 to 60 days it is decided by urinalysis and, if that is negative, by inflammatory markers.
caption: Pathway after the AAP 2021 guideline on well-appearing febrile infants 8–60 days; the under-8-day and ill-appearing infant is outside it.

nodes.text: Febrile infant under 60 days, temperature 38.0 °C or more
Well-appearing, term, 8 days or older, no comorbidity?
Full evaluation including LP, IV antibiotics, admit
LP routine with full evaluation; empiric antibiotics and admission
LP with full evaluation; if CSF and markers normal, observe or treat
29 to 60 days: urinalysis and urine culture first
Treat as UTI: blood culture, antibiotics; LP if markers abnormal
No LP, no antibiotics; follow-up and recheck within 24 hours
Perform LP and blood culture; empiric antibiotics; admit or observe
Defer LP if unstable, coagulopathic or infected skin at site; give antibiotics
